sender.en: A “recruiter” from a freelancing platform, then someone claiming to be police or FIA

name.en: Fake freelancing job group, then “police” blackmail: “you shared illegal content, pay or face a case”

how.en: A fake recruiter offers freelancing work or training and adds you to a WhatsApp or Telegram group that looks professional. Explicit content is then posted in the group, and people who react or forward it are later contacted by someone posing as law enforcement. They accuse you of sharing illegal material and demand large sums, reported at Rs 1 to 1.5 million, to avoid a case and public shame. National CERT warned that this targets young people and freelancers, especially in Punjab.

text.en: A recruiter offers freelancing work and adds you to a group.
Explicit content appears in the group.
A “police officer” contacts you and accuses you of sharing it.
They demand a large payment to drop the case and keep it quiet.
Hello! We are hiring freelancers for online data entry, earn Rs 5,000 daily from home. Join our training group: [link]
This is Inspector from Cyber Crime. You forwarded illegal videos from a WhatsApp group. An FIR will be registered and your family will be informed unless you settle the matter today.

en: freelancing whatsapp group explicit videos then police call
fake recruiter added me to whatsapp group
caller said i shared illegal content pay money
cyber crime officer demanding money to avoid fir
Job offers that put you in groups with strangers.
Any “officer” who settles a case for money over the phone.
Leave any group that shares explicit content; don’t forward or save it.
Set WhatsApp so only your contacts can add you to groups.
Don’t pay; report to NCCIA on 1799, and call 15 if threatened.

sources.title: Warnings issued over WhatsApp scams targeting Pakistani users with fake job offers, extortion threats
